articles.title: US raises alarm over American detained in China
articles.summary: 🌎 Plus: Darline Graham tries to clean up debate gaffe {beacon} It’s Thursday, and we’ve got some big news from Cate Martel! Your usual 12:30 correspondent welcomed a new baby, Liam, and is out for the next few months on maternity leave! 🍼👶 Programming note: We will have a rotating cast of Hill folks taking the reins while she’s out.…
articles.body:
It’s Thursday, and we’ve got some big news from Cate Martel !

Your usual 12:30 correspondent welcomed a new baby, Liam, and is out for the next few months on maternity leave! 🍼👶

Programming note: We will have a rotating cast of Hill folks taking the reins while she’s out. For today, we’re Abigail Walker and Claire Leibowitz . Please send your tips, comments and story ideas to awalker@thehill.com or cleibowitz@thehill.com .

US officials raise alarm over citizen imprisoned in China

Army can’t make up its mind on cadet standards

Sparks are still flying after the Ossoff-Trump-Harp drama

Sean Duffy says Harvard can corrupt ‘young girls’

Darline Graham defends national security stumble

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex return to the U.K.

An American citizen who runs a think tank focused on politics in Myanmar was arrested in China, and U.S. officials are now highlighting the “significant deterioration” in his treatment.

What happened?: Min Zin was arrested in June, but U.S. officials on Thursday designated him as “wrongfully detained,” a powerful label “that makes advocating for his release a top U.S. priority,” The Hill’s Laura Kelly reports .

He had a 10-year visa to enter China and frequently attended academic conferences in the country. He was detained upon his arrival on June 3, accused of spying and endangering China’s national security.

How is he being treated?: Zin is being held at an unknown location, which means U.S. consular officials cannot observe his living conditions and can only see him when Chinese officials bring him to a hotel. He was placed at the opposite end of a long conference table during the last conversation, making communication difficult.

Not normal: “Chinese authorities barred U.S. officials from discussing with Min Zin any questions related to his case, interrogation, treatment, his work on Myanmar or his colleagues,” Kelly writes. “A consular officer, who has dealt with Americans detained in China for more than two years, called it one of the most disruptive and restrictive visits he’s ever experienced, according to the account.”

Officials are also concerned about Chinese authorities blocking basic humanitarian care for Zin, including blocking reading materials and keeping him in constant light, blocking his ability to sleep.

On the agenda: President Trump is expected to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping for a state visit on Sept. 24.

Zin’s family and friends hope the escalation to “wrongfully detained” and Trump’s attention will secure his release.

🔎 Insiders can read the rest of Laura Kelly’s reporting here .

“The Army is eyeing new minimum academic standards for college students in the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC), but not without some internal drama,” The Hill’s Filip Timotija reports .

The service branch issued the changes earlier this month but pulled them only days later.

What was withdrawn?: Incoming ROTC cadets — undergrad students — would have to meet one of three academic benchmarks: a 20 on the ACT, a 1000 on the SAT or a result in the 50th percentile on the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery, a standardized test on science, math and language.

Where did they go?: A memo reviewed by The Hill said the standards required “further staffing and analysis,” and there was apparently a lack of consultation with senior leaders.

^ Read the New York Post’s report on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s reaction: ‘Hegseth angry as Army scraps new SAT minimum meant to screen out ‘stupid’ officers’

This comes as Hegseth has emphasized a focus on fitness and grooming for service members.

“Backers of the Aug. 5 memo say cadets should show intellectual agility before becoming officers. Others question if ACTs and SATs are reliable measures to assess an officer’s future performance,” Timotija writes.

Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) might take the cake for causing the longest news cycle with the fewest words. Maybe because it’s August, but he sure did rankle Trump world.

“He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the emir of Qatar,” Ossoff said during a Georgia rally last weekend, referring to the president’s executive assistant, Natalie Harp.

The comment got a roar from the crowd and continues to reverberate on social media. Trump’s allies have ripped into Ossoff for comments they call sexist and reckless.

His son, Eric Trump , swatted back at the critics , calling speculation about his father’s relationship with Harp “absolute trash.”

“Natalie is an incredible young woman — a cancer survivor, a genuinely good person, and arguably one of the hardest-working people in the White House. She’s deeply committed to my father, to her job, and to this country,” he said in a post on the social platform X.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle chose to poke fun at Ossoff , describing the senator as a “cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama.”

Should he really be saying this? Trump allies weren’t the only ones who found the comments to be in poor taste.

Democratic strategist David Axelrod wasn’t impressed by Ossoff’s comments either.

“No one has been more consistently eloquent or incisive in exposing @realDonaldTrump than @Ossoff,” he wrote. “The paragraph from his weekend speech that has gotten so much attention was a brutal takedown. But two words in it, ‘with Natalie’ seemed gratuitous and unnecessary.”

DUFFY FAMILY VALUES : Harvard University is no place for young women with conservative, Catholic values. At least that’s what Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy implied during the second episode of “Great American Road Trip,” a series on the department’s YouTube page, which centered on Boston, Massachusetts.

“If I send you there, I think what happens is they have professionalized figuring out how they can take good, young girls like you, and I think, corrupt their minds,” he said to his daughter, Paloma, after she expressed interest in attending the prestigious institution.

Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) on Wednesday tried to defend her lackluster performance earlier this week in a primary runoff debate.

When asked Tuesday night if and why the South China Sea and Taiwan were a national security issue for the U.S., Graham candidly responded , “I’m not that informed on national security.” She then paused before saying, “But I do support the military.”

Not impressed : Former South Carolina state Rep. Adam Morgan (R) reacted to the stumble, calling it a “stunning debate flop” and insisting on X that Graham is “not qualified for this 6-year position.”

“I tripped up on one question last night regarding Taiwan,” Graham said during a Fox News interview yesterday. “I have said many times I’m not a politician, certainly not a career politician. I don’t speak politician.”

But…she is definitely a politician : Following the death of her brother Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) last month, Darline Graham was appointed by South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster (R) to serve out the remainder the late senator’s fourth term.

Graham is now vying for the full-time job . Though backed by the president and the Republican National Committee, she must still convince South Carolinians that she’s prepared to fill her brother’s shoes.

“Lindsey Graham was well informed on the United States’ national security,” former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley wrote on X. “Darline Graham admits she’s not. This is not something you inherit. And it’s critical in the U.S. Senate.”

— Secretary of State Marco Rubio outperformed Vice President Vance in multiple hypothetical 2028 match-ups against Democrats. The Emerson College and The Hill poll pitted them against former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, who was the only Democrat to hold a lead against the two. Ossoff, California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D), former Vice President Kamala Harris and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) all trailed behind Rubio. Ocasio-Cortez was the only one to (hypothetically) lose to both Republicans.

— Poll mania: Another survey found that Republicans are trailing Democrats by 8 points on a generic congressional ballot. Half of respondents said they would back a Democrat if the midterm elections were held that day, 43 percent said they would back a Republican and 6.3 percent were unsure.

— Young Democrats are vying for Congress , putting affordability at the top of their agenda. Darializa Avila Chevalier in New York’s 13th Congressional District, Angela Gonzales-Torres in California’s 34th Congressional District and Melat Kiros in Colorado’s 1st Congressional District, among others, have shown little hesitation in making the high cost of living a key part of their campaigns.

Politico: EU backs top international court against Rubio

AP News: US agency under scrutiny after watchdog warns of forced labor in Dominican Republic

Reuters: US envoy Huckabee tells Israeli settlers not to take Palestinian Americans’ land

NOTUS: Judge Blocks Trump’s Abstinence-Only Overhaul of Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program

The House and Senate are out. President Trump is in Washington. (All times EDT)

2 p.m. Trump participates in signing time.

4 p.m. Trump and first lady Melania Trump make a “Fostering the Future” announcement in the Rose Garden.

🥓 Celebrate : Today is National Bacon Lovers Day!

👑 We hope the Duke and Duchess of Sussex stock up. Prince Harry and Meghan are moving back to the U.K. after six years in America. Of course, bacon is a key component of an English breakfast, but we’re confident it’s better on this side of the pond.

B ecause you made it this far, here’s a pup enjoying the wind and the waves . Start booking your weekend plans — hopefully they look something like this.

articles.title: CNN is obsessed with Natalie Harp, shamefully interviews brother
articles.summary: t’s just bad form, and awkward, to induce family members of public figures to criticize them, unless they’re telling us something we need to know and couldn’t have learned any other way.
articles.body:
“OutFront” host Erin Burnett interviewed the brother of Natalie Harp, the Trump aide who is suddenly under scrutiny after Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff implied there was some sort of inappropriate closeness there. Harp’s brother, Preston Harp, is estranged from her, and is not a public figure or notable person whatsoever, nor does he actually have firsthand knowledge about Harp’s relationship with President Trump. I repeat, they are estranged.

Those details all make Preston Harp a highly unsuitable figure for an interview on a national news program. It’s just bad form, and awkward, to induce family members of public figures to criticize them, unless they’re telling us something we need to know and couldn’t have learned any other way. That’s clearly not the case here. The interview comes off as very weird and obsessed with Harp in a gossipy sort of way.

It then veers into even more bizarre territory, as Preston Harp details his sister’s alleged infatuation with Trump , and Burnett drills down on that term.

I’m sorry, but there’s something sleazy about that. It’s like they’re trying to lead viewers to the conclusion that there’s something inappropriate about the relationship when, again, no one has presented a shred of evidence that this is the case. It’s all just projection and innuendo.

I think that’s unethical. It’s unethical for a journalist to try to leave her viewers with the impression that maybe there’s reason to think this young woman is having an affair with her boss, the president of the United States. It’s also morally suspect to involve the woman’s own brother in this effort.

Again, to be clear, if there was something going on, then yes, it would be news, and they could interview someone about it, although I still think the brother would be a weird choice. But it’s not news, because there’s no evidence. Yet mainstream media journalists feel totally justified to smear Natalie Harp.

Julie Brown, a reporter for The Miami Herald known for her sensationalist reporting on the Epstein files, referred to Harp as Trump’s side piece . Gross, gross stuff. Responding to the interview, Laura Loomer writes on X : “According to the media, being loyal to your boss is an “unhealthy obsession.”

She continues: “Everyone should wish they had an executive assistant as dedicated as Natalie Harp. Natalie is great. These stories will only make POTUS like her more. The media is beyond desperate.”

Beyond desperate indeed. But they just can’t help themselves.

Robby Soave is co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising” and a senior editor for Reason Magazine. This column is an edited transcription of his daily commentary.

articles.title: Joe Rogan on democratic socialists’ ideology: ‘It sucks’
articles.summary: Joe Rogan said Wednesday that democratic socialists’ entire ideology “sucks” and accused those supporting the progressive movement of being “Marxists” fueled by what he described as manipulative social media rhetoric. “It sucks. … People are really [arguing], ‘Oh maybe being socialist is cool.’ Like, this is all coming out of social media. One hundred percent,”…
articles.body:
Joe Rogan said Wednesday that democratic socialists’ entire ideology “sucks” and accused those supporting the progressive movement of being “Marxists” fueled by what he described as manipulative social media rhetoric.

“It sucks. … People are really [arguing], ‘Oh maybe being socialist is cool.’ Like, this is all coming out of social media. One hundred percent,” Rogan said during the latest episode of his podcast.

“It’s not natural that people are sitting around reading Marx and going, ‘What a great idea, let’s implement this.’ They’re not doing that,” he added.

Last month, President Trump shared a video calling for “hardcore communist bastards” to be deported, notably naming New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) as part of the political grouping. He similarly described Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D), who does not identify as a democratic socialist, as a “Communist loser who hates Jews and Israel.”

Trump also said communism is “ the greatest threat to our country in history ” — including World War I, World War II and the attack on Pearl Harbor — and frequently uses the political ideology to attack progressive Democratic candidates.

While socialism is tied to Marxism , they are not the same thing.

Socialism is a wide-ranging term for any system where the public owns and controls means of production (like factories, land and tools) to meet human needs instead of the private sector.

Marxism is a specific theoretical system created by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels that uses “historical materialist” analysis to study class struggle, economic structures and the inevitable collapse of capitalism.

On Wednesday, Rogan said, “Very few of these quote unquote Marxists that you find on social media are even aware of the consequences, the historical consequences of these strategies and what it ultimately leads to.”

He added, “It’s like checkers, it’s like real simple: You’re going to have a military that controls everything you do . As soon as you give up everything to the state, well the state has the guns and you have nothing and they tell you what to do.”

His guest, conservative commentator Steve Hilton, responded to Rogan by highlighting the impact of Marxism-Leninism in the Soviet Union.

Hilton said state-run grocery stores in Hungary under Soviet rule were “terrible.” During this era, the communist country adopted a heavily modified version of Marxism adapted by Vladimir Lenin and later codified by Joseph Stalin — which prioritized a powerful central state over the stateless society Marx proposed.

Hilton’s comments were made in response to Mamdani’s proposal for government-run grocery stores to promote affordability. The mayor has not identified himself as a Marxist or a communist, though.

However, those who criticize his political policies have labeled him as such — also claiming the mayor would facilitate a sharp turn to a factionless society from a thriving capitalist economy.

The targeted attacks from Republicans — and efforts from establishment Democrats to separate themselves from their progressive counterparts — come as democratic socialists gain ground in congressional races by winning primaries, ousting incumbents and fueling their base with grassroots support for their nominees.

New York and Colorado welcomed democratic socialists as the party nominee in several primaries earlier this summer, while a progressive similarly claimed Michigan’s Democratic nomination for the Senate and a center-left nominee barely beat out his democratic socialist opponent in Wisconsin’s widely covered gubernatorial primary.

Some strategists say the Democratic Party needs to unite in order to regain the majority in the House this fall and embrace an integrated messaging on affordability.

“With major battleground state primaries, like Wisconsin and Michigan, behind us, Democrats now need to unite around one overriding priority: defeating MAGA Republicans, winning back governing power, and making it far harder for Donald Trump to continue advancing a harmful agenda over the final two years of his presidency,” National Democratic Training Committee Founder and CEO Kelly Dietrich told The Hill.

“This will only happen, though, if Democrats stay focused on the kitchen-table issues that deeply matter to everyday Americans — lowering costs at the grocery store and gas pumps and holding the Trump administration accountable for this reckless, deadly, unnecessary war that is only driving prices higher,” he added.

articles.title: ‘Doesn’t wanna win’: Charlamagne Tha God bashes Hakeem Jeffries over healthcare
articles.summary: if a political leader as powerful as Hakeem Jeffries changes position on a major issue, voters deserve more than a pivot. They deserve the why and, more importantly, the what now.
articles.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is facing criticism after a recent exchange on “Meet the Press” where he said he does not support Medicare for All.

It’s getting attention because Jeffries previously supported and co-sponsored the legislation in 2019.

And that’s where Charlamagne Tha God comes in, giving Jeffries his Donkey of the Day, going directly after the change in Jeffries’s position.

Voters want government involved in healthcare. Don’t take my word for it: a 2025 Data for Progress poll found 65 percent of likely voters supported Medicare for All when it was described as replacing most private insurance.

But Pew found something broader: 66 percent of Americans said the federal government has a responsibility to ensure everyone has health coverage .

And the affordability problem is also a real one.

KFF found 36 percent of adults said they skipped or postponed needed healthcare because of cost. So, if a political leader as powerful as Hakeem Jeffries changes position on a major issue, voters deserve more than a pivot. They deserve the why and, more importantly, the what now.

If Medicare for All is no longer the answer, what is? Because if memory serves me correctly, the government shut down a few months back over rising healthcare costs , and since then, nothing has changed. In fact, health costs have only gone up !

Do the new options Jeffries has in mind offer lower premiums, cheaper prescriptions or protection from medical debt? We have been fighting about lackluster healthcare options for decades in this country.

Americans are already paying the price of a healthcare system they believe is broken. Blaming the other party alone doesn’t answer the question all voters are asking at this point: What exactly is your solution?

Lindsey Granger is a NewsNation contributor and co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising.” This column is an edited transcription of her on-air commentary.

articles.title: ‘Reading Rainbow’ host says he’s checking into hospital over mental health
articles.summary: Threets was tapped as the host of “Reading Rainbow” in 2025, replacing original host LeVar Burton.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — The host of the “ Reading Rainbow ” reboot is prioritizing his mental health.

Mychal Threets wrote on Threads earlier this week that he would be checking himself into the hospital to seek treatment.

“I am not okay. Maybe I’ll never be okay. I’m seeking help,” he said. “Going to the hospital tomorrow. In this moment I am safe. By God’s grace.”

He added, “No matter what happens to me, I will always be thankful for the extraordinary people in my life who worry, who help me. Thank you for your care. I will always love you.”

The librarian and author received support underneath his post.

“Community” actress Yvette Nicole Brown advised , “If you need the help, maybe go tonight, friend.”

This image released by Embassy Row shows literacy advocate Mychal Threets, host of the children’s series “Reading Rainbow” on the KidZuko YouTube channel. (Embassy Row via AP)

Another Threads user said, “Mychael, please get the help that you need because this world is a better place because you’re in it.”

“Please take care of yourself. You are loved by so many people,” another person wrote . “Most of us who haven’t even met you but admire all that you stand for. Please keep on living. We need you so much!”

Threets has been open about his mental health struggles.

After going viral in 2023 for sharing uplifting messages on his TikTok and Instagram pages and gaining a large following, Threets resigned from his librarian role at a library in California in 2024 after struggling with his mental health.

“I was just really struggling in life, struggling at work for the first time, just started feeling burnt out,” he told NBC Bay Area at the time, adding that he contemplated suicide.

Threets was tapped as the host of “Reading Rainbow” in 2025, replacing original host LeVar Burton .

The first iteration of “Reading Rainbow” aired on PBS from 1983 to 2006.

articles.title: Democrats to decide among Boston, Denver, Philadelphia for 2028 convention
articles.summary: Democrats on Thursday narrowed down their top three cities for the 2028 national convention, spotlighting Boston, Denver and Philadelphia as viable options for the party to introduce its presidential nominee. “Each city presented strong bids to host an inspiring celebration of our party’s future nominee and a critical step on our path to retaking the…
articles.body:
Democrats on Thursday narrowed down their top three cities for the 2028 national convention, spotlighting Boston, Denver and Philadelphia as viable options for the party to introduce its presidential nominee.

“Each city presented strong bids to host an inspiring celebration of our party’s future nominee and a critical step on our path to retaking the White House,” Democratic National Committee (DNC) Chair Ken Martin wrote in a post on social platform X .

“We look forward to continuing to work with them as the DNC makes a final selection over the coming months,” he added.

It’s been 10 years since Philadelphia last hosted the convention in 2016 followed by the 2008 convention in Denver and a 2004 stop in Boston.

Officials with the Democratic Party visited all three locations earlier this year in April and May alongside Atlanta and Chicago, which were knocked off the final list of potential sites.

The three selected cities offer broad insight into whose attention the party is looking to capture in the next presidential election.

Denver has been home to a growing progressive faction within the party, made evident by democratic socialist Melat Kiros, who beat incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette (D-Colo.) in the June primary.

Meanwhile, Boston has a strong blue donor base and is in one of the states former Vice President Kamala Harris won in the 2024 presidential election. It’s also widely known as the “birthplace of American values” with deep ties to the foundation of the country’s democracy.

President Trump won the state of Pennsylvania in the last presidential election and also survived an assassination attempt in Butler, which drove political fanfare for the leader ahead of his return to the White House.

Harris failed to capture Black male voters in the city of “brotherly love,” but Democrats now have a chance to solidify support in the crucial swing state with an organized labor backbone tied to the union workforce.

Martin is expected to finalize the city for the 2028 Democratic National Convention in the coming months.

However, he faced extreme pushback from Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens (D) for not selecting the city as one of the final options for the party’s convention.

Dickens said the measure was an attempt to abandon the South and Black voters, despite Democrats’ recent decision to keep South Carolina as the first in the nation primary for the party.

articles.title: Bipartisan women call on Ethics panel to speed up Gomez probe ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Female lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are calling for the House Ethics Committee to speed up its investigation into sexual misconduct allegations against Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) ahead of the midterms. The House Ethics Committee on Monday said it was investigating allegations that Gomez violated House rules by “engaging in inappropriate sexual contact…
articles.body:
Female lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are calling for the House Ethics Committee to speed up its investigation into sexual misconduct allegations against Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) ahead of the midterms.

The House Ethics Committee on Monday said it was investigating allegations that Gomez violated House rules by “engaging in inappropriate sexual contact with a House staffer.”

CNN reported in June that the committee was investigating Gomez, after the New York Post published a story that said he was seen kissing a younger staffer who worked for a different House Democrat in 2023.

The Democratic Women’s Caucus on Wednesday called on the Ethics Committee to “release the status of their investigation, while protecting survivor privacy, before the 60-day blackout period ahead of Election Day.”

“The recent allegations against Representative Jimmy Gomez are disturbing and must be taken seriously. Allegations of workplace sexual harassment against women must be investigated and if substantiated, met with clear and meaningful consequences,” Democratic Reps. Teresa Leger Fernández (N.M.), Emilia Sykes (Ohio) and Hillary Scholten (Mich.) wrote in a statement.

Leger Fernández is the chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, while Sykes and Scholten serve as vice chairs.

Rep. Kat Cammack (R-Fla.), chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, said in a statement the committee “should move with urgency, and if these allegations are substantiated, Representative Gomez must resign and any criminal conduct must be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.”

Gomez told The Hill in a previous statement his actions “were consensual in nature and haven’t violated the law or House Ethics rules.”

But two attorneys said Wednesday their client told the House Ethics Committee that Gomez sexually harassed and assaulted her.

“Contrary to Representative Gomez’s assertion in his statement, his actions were not ‘consensual in nature’ with respect to our client,” wrote the attorneys, Lisa Banks and Sarah Nesbitt of Katz Banks Kumin LLP, in a joint statement. “We fully expect that the House Committee on Ethics will come to the same conclusion in its investigation.”

Cammack said the woman “showed real courage” in telling the committee about her experience.

“She deserves a process that is fast, fair, and fearless. Due process must be respected, but it cannot be used to run out the clock,” the Florida Republican said.

articles.title: Rosie O’Donnell jabs Trump, fuels Harp buzz: ‘Let Natalie tuck you in’
articles.summary: Comedian Rosie O’Donnell swiped at President Trump over his close relationship with his executive assistant Natalie Harp while guest-hosting ABC’s “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” Wednesday, piling on to the viral critique of the longtime White House aide. “A special hello to those of you watching from home and from the White House,” O’Donnell said during her…
articles.body:
Comedian Rosie O’Donnell swiped at President Trump over his close relationship with his executive assistant Natalie Harp while guest-hosting ABC’s “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” Wednesday, piling on to the viral critique of the longtime White House aide.

“A special hello to those of you watching from home and from the White House,” O’Donnell said during her monologue, while not mentioning Trump’s name directly. “But I do have some bad news for President Petty Roosevelt. That’s all I’m going to say about you tonight, sweetheart.”

O’Donnell, who has feuded with Trump for years, opened her third night filling in for Jimmy Kimmel by joking that she would leave the president alone for the night, before turning her attention to Harp.

“You’ve got to realize it’s time to hang up your wig and let Natalie tuck you in,” O’Donnell said, drawing gasps and applause from the audience. “Time to go nighty night.”

Harp, a longtime Trump aide who has reportedly accompanied the president on his golf trips and to his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida on a regular basis, has been in the center of media headlines since Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) slammed her during a campaign speech Sunday .

Ossoff, who is seeking reelection against Trump-backed Rep. Mike Collins (R-Ga.), fired at Trump over his planned White ballroom construction and a luxury jet donated by Qatar, saying the president “wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace.”

Several key figures in Trump’s inner circle have come to Harp’s defense , including the president’s son Eric Trump, who called Ossoff’s comments “absolute trash,” and White House Communications Director Steven Cheung who fired back at the Georgia Democrat.

“Instead of denigrating hard-working people serving their country, Jon should look deep into his soul and ask himself why he’s a miserable person who hates this country,” Cheung wrote on social media, adding, “It’s because he’s a radical, extremist Dumocrat,” using Trump’s nickname for Democrats.

articles.title: Cook Political Report moves Iowa, Texas governor’s races in Democrats favor
articles.summary: The nonpartisan Cook Political Report shifted its ratings Thursday for both the Texas and Iowa gubernatorial races, giving Democrats a higher chance at claiming the seat. Jessica Taylor, Cook Political Report’s Senate and governors editor, wrote in her analysis that Texas’s Democratic nominee for governor, state Rep. Gina Hinojosa (D), is “surprisingly competitive” against incumbent…
articles.body:
The nonpartisan Cook Political Report shifted its ratings Thursday for both the Texas and Iowa gubernatorial races, giving Democrats a higher chance at claiming the seat.

Jessica Taylor, Cook Political Report’s Senate and governors editor, wrote in her analysis that Texas’s Democratic nominee for governor, state Rep. Gina Hinojosa (D), is “surprisingly competitive” against incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott (R). The political analyst also labeled Senate races in both states “toss-ups” — a shift from “lean Republican.”

Cook Political Reported shifted its Texas gubernatorial race predictions to “likely Republican” from “solid Republican” after Hinojosa launched ads attacking Abbott for accepting money from data centers. Though Cook’s analysis also said Hinojosa needs to “substantially” up her fundraising efforts “to be truly competitive come November.”

An Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media survey , released in August, found that 49 percent of likely voters supported Abbott, while 45 percent backed Hinojosa.

If Abbott wins in November, he will become the longest serving governor in the state’s history and continue a 30-year streak of Republicans holding the office.

The Iowa gubernatorial race was rated a “toss-up” in April but shifted to “lean Democrat” in the report’s most recent analysis. Taylor added that the Democratic nominee, Iowa state auditor Rob Sand, has been opening a “consistent lead outside of the margin of error in both public and private polling” against GOP nominee Zach Lahn.

Another August Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media survey of Iowa voters found 48 percent supported Sand while 43 percent supported Lahn. The survey had a margin of error of 3.7 percentage points.

Sand is currently the only member of his party to hold a statewide office in Iowa, and the state has not had a Democratic governor for two decades.

While running for state auditor, Sand catered to Republican and independent voters — emphasizing his bowhunter past and saying he’d be willing to stand up against his party if he opposed an issue. In this year’s election, Lahn has campaigned on his background as a six-generation Iowan and positioned himself as an antiestablishment Republican candidate.

Cook does not expect the gubernatorial race “to be a blowout” for Democrats due to the state’s voting history, according to its most recent report, though it still sees “an edge” for the party in some of its prominent races.

articles.title: Watch: Trump, first lady headline Fostering Future Together event in Rose Garden
articles.summary: First lady Melania Trump, joined by President Trump, made an announcement at the White House Rose Garden on Thursday afternoon related to the administration’s Fostering the Future Together initiative. While details surrounding the event were slim, the initiative has looked to expand academic opportunities for young people transitioning out of the foster care system. The…
articles.body:
First lady Melania Trump, joined by President Trump, made an announcement at the White House Rose Garden on Thursday afternoon related to the administration’s Fostering the Future Together initiative.

While details surrounding the event were slim, the initiative has looked to expand academic opportunities for young people transitioning out of the foster care system . The New York Post reported Thursday morning that the Trumps planned to announce a new scholarship.

Their remarks came ahead of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix , slated for Saturday and Sunday in the nation’s capital. The 1.7-mile course will loop around the National Archives, National Gallery of Art and Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, according to a map released Monday.

IndyCar officials attended Thursday’s event.

articles.title: Another polling firm comes under fire for ‘falsified data’ on Florida primary
articles.summary: A major polling tracker announced Thursday it would suspend its use of data from a pollster after it discovered evidence that the firm allegedly “falsified data” in a survey of candidates in Florida’s gubernatorial Republican primary race. The decision follows a shocking announcement last week from fake polling center Median Strategies, which admitted to spreading…
articles.body:
A major polling tracker announced Thursday it would suspend its use of data from a pollster after it discovered evidence that the firm allegedly “falsified data” in a survey of candidates in Florida’s gubernatorial Republican primary race.

The decision follows a shocking announcement last week from fake polling center Median Strategies, which admitted to spreading false polling data on the Los Angeles mayoral race as part of a “short-term social experiment” on the spread of unverified information.

FiftyPlusOne announced Thursday it was “permanently banning” its use of The Public Sentiment Institute’s (TPSI) data after the firm reportedly fabricated vote-choice data for select respondents in their survey and failed to disclose it was funded by James Fishback’s campaign , one of the GOP candidates in the Florida gubernatorial race.

“This fabrication appears to have boosted the poll numbers of the political candidate that paid TPSI for polling services,” the firm wrote.

While TPSI took responsibility for not disclosing the funding source behind this poll, it pushed back on the accusations of data manipulation.

“No respondent was removed, no response was altered, and no data was fabricated,” the firm told The Hill in a statement. “When the raw data was reprocessed following the election, it reproduced the same measurements, and every candidate’s raw response share fell within the applicable margin of error of the certified results.”

Instead, TPSI said in its “ accuracy review ” of the survey that an error occurred after the firm applied an “experimental layer” that applied previous survey results to the poll after its results “did not align with our read of the race.”

“Acting on that conclusion, we identified respondents who selected [Florida Lt. Gov Jay] Collins but whose broader profile aligned with a competing coalition, and leaned those respondents toward James Fishback,” the firm wrote in this document.

This change drove Fishback to second place in the poll behind Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.), booting Collins to the third-place spot. Donalds defeated both candidates in the state’s GOP primary on Tuesday.

The firm explained that the experimental layer involved in this error is now “discontinued and will not appear in any future TPSI release” in its review.

“We accept responsibility for both the disclosure failure and the methodological error,” the polling tracker told The Hill. “We do not accept the characterization that either amounts to deliberate data falsification, and the underlying record does not support that conclusion.”

Austin Park, the co-founder and head of research at VoteHub, noted that his firm’s tracker has already “excluded” TPSI data from its averages for several months.

“The American Association for Public Opinion Research just released a statement on fabricated polling following the Median Strategies issue,” Park wrote on social media . “Disappointing to see TPSI effectively fabricate their data as well.”

Additionally, FiftyPlusOne said Thursday it would temporarily suspend the use of data from another firm, Patriot Polling, due to concerns that they also failed to disclose Fishback’s campaign as a sponsor behind their poll in this race.

“We have discovered evidence that suggests both firms conducted surveys for political campaigns without disclosing their clients publicly,” the organization said in a statement on their website.

“All surveys from each pollster that exist in our database at publication will be marked as partisan, as we cannot be confident, they were conducted on a nonpartisan basis as the pollsters claim,” it continued.

The Hill has reached out to Patriot Polling for comment.

While TPSI took responsibility for not disclosing the funding source behind this poll, it pushed back on the accusations of data manipulation.

“No respondent was removed, no response was altered, and no data was fabricated,” the firm told The Hill in a statement. “When the raw data was reprocessed following the election, it reproduced the same measurements, and every candidate’s raw response share fell within the applicable margin of error of the certified results.”

Instead, TPSI said in its “ accuracy review ” of the survey that an error occurred after the firm applied an “experimental layer” that applied previous survey results to the poll after its results “did not align with our read of the race.”

“Acting on that conclusion, we identified respondents who selected [Florida Lt. Gov Jay] Collins but whose broader profile aligned with a competing coalition, and leaned those respondents toward James Fishback,” the firm wrote in this document.

This change drove Fishback to second place in the poll behind Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.), booting Collins to the third-place spot. Donalds defeated both candidates in the state’s GOP primary on Tuesday.
The firm explained that the experimental layer involved in this error is now “discontinued and will not appear in any future TPSI release” in its review.

“We accept responsibility for both the disclosure failure and the methodological error,” the polling tracker told The Hill. “We do not accept the characterization that either amounts to deliberate data falsification, and the underlying record does not support that conclusion.”
Austin Park, the co-founder and head of research at VoteHub, noted that his firm’s tracker has already “excluded” TPSI data from its averages for several months.

“The American Association for Public Opinion Research just released a statement on fabricated polling following the Median Strategies issue,” Park wrote on social media . “Disappointing to see TPSI effectively fabricate their data as well.”

Additionally, FiftyPlusOne said Thursday it would temporarily suspend the use of data from another firm, Patriot Polling, due to concerns that they also failed to disclose Fishback’s campaign as a sponsor behind their poll in this race.
“We have discovered evidence that suggests both firms conducted surveys for political campaigns without disclosing their clients publicly,” the organization said in a statement on their website.

“All surveys from each pollster that exist in our database at publication will be marked as partisan, as we cannot be confident, they were conducted on a nonpartisan basis as the pollsters claim,” it continued.
The Hill has reached out to Patriot Polling for comment.

articles.title: Gabbard shares emotional update on husband’s cancer months after White House exit
articles.summary: Tulsi Gabbard, the former director of National Intelligence, shared a new update Thursday on her husband’s battle with a rare form of bone cancer, months after she announced that her resignation from the Trump administration was prompted by his diagnosis. “Earlier this year, my husband Abraham was diagnosed with a very rare bone cancer,” Gabbard…
articles.body:
Tulsi Gabbard, the former director of National Intelligence, shared a new update Thursday on her husband’s battle with a rare form of bone cancer, months after she announced that her resignation from the Trump administration was prompted by his diagnosis.

“Earlier this year, my husband Abraham was diagnosed with a very rare bone cancer,” Gabbard said in a video shared to social media Thursday. “This has been a very challenging time for us and is hard to talk about.”

Her husband was diagnosed earlier this year with sacral chordoma and has since undergone surgery to remove the tumor and surrounding tissue. She shared clips of her husband in the hospital as he prepared to go into surgery, which was successful .

“So many of you have reached out asking how he’s doing and sharing your prayers and well wishes with us,” she said. “We made this video to share a little about what this journey has been like and to update you on his recovery.”

The video shows clips of her husband, a cinematographer who she married in 2015, learning to walk again after the surgery. Gabbard shared that the recovery process was “scary,” which she said she did not expect, and that her husband refused to take any narcotic pain medication.

“A few weeks after the surgery was done, pathologists and the doctor said that they were confident that they were able to cut out all of the cancerous bone and tissue,” she said in the video.

Gabbard added that in the nearly three months since the successful operation, her husband has started “very rigorous physical therapy” and overall is “progressing very well.”

“The reality is that the battle isn’t over yet,” she said, adding that her husband will need to continue receiving frequent MRIs to ensure the cancer does not come back.

She was later joined by her husband at the end of the video, and the two shared a tearful hug.

Gabbard first disclosed her husband’s diagnosis in May when she announced her resignation, saying he would face “major challenges in the coming weeks and months.”

“At this time, I must step away from public service to be by his side and fully support him through this battle,” she wrote in her resignation letter to President Trump.

Gabbard officially left the administration in June after serving as director of National Intelligence for 16 months.

articles.title: GOP, Democrats lament $40 trillion debt as Congress struggles to act
articles.summary: Lawmakers are sounding the alarm over the nation’s $40 trillion debt, lamenting Congress’s inability to meaningfully confront a problem that has grown increasingly difficult to ignore. Both parties have spent years trying to tackle the rising debt. Republicans have frequently pointed to federal spending and entitlement programs as the main drivers, while Democrats have emphasized…
articles.body:
Lawmakers are sounding the alarm over the nation’s $40 trillion debt, lamenting Congress’s inability to meaningfully confront a problem that has grown increasingly difficult to ignore.

Both parties have spent years trying to tackle the rising debt. Republicans have frequently pointed to federal spending and entitlement programs as the main drivers, while Democrats have emphasized the need for higher taxes on wealthy Americans and corporations alongside spending reforms.

But efforts to reach a broader deal have repeatedly stalled as both parties have balked at the politically painful trade-offs needed to put the nation on a more sustainable fiscal path.

After the debt officially hit $40 trillion Wednesday, lawmakers took to social media to argue for policies that would soothe the debt. The milestone figure comes after years of federal borrowing that accelerated during the pandemic and remained elevated as Congress continued to approve large spending packages and tax policies.

“This is bad,” Sen. Rick Scott (R-Fla.) said in a post on social platform X . “Congress needs to get spending under control and BALANCE THE BUDGET.”

Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.), a fiscal conservative like Scott, also blamed politicians for not balancing the federal budget.

“Instead of paying for things as we go, Washington spends and spends,” Paul said. “You and your family make a budget and live by it. Washington should as well.”

Members of the far-right House Freedom Caucus, who typically advocate for spending cuts, also quickly called for Congress to crack down on waste, fraud and abuse in federal spending.

“America’s national debt has officially crossed a line that should alarm every single American. This is not just another number. It is a flashing warning sign that Washington’s reckless, unchecked spending is putting the future of our country, and generations of Americans, at risk,” Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.), a member of the caucus, wrote in a post online .

“We cannot tax our way out of this. We cannot keep borrowing our way out of this. Congress MUST find the backbone to make the tough decisions, rein in spending, and get our fiscal house in order,” he added.

Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah), in a post on X , called the debt problem “immoral” and called for legislation like the Fiscal Commission Act, which would establish a commission on fiscal responsibility and reform in the federal government. Curtis said this would be “a good start.”

“Our reckless spending problem in Washington is immoral—it unfairly leaves our children and grandchildren to foot the bill—but it also is making our economic stability extremely fragile,” Curtis said. “The more we add to our debt, the greater the threat of disaster in the event of an economic shock.”

Republicans are weighing a third reconciliation package that will likely only add to concerns about the nation’s debt trajectory.

The package President Trump and GOP leaders are hoping to pass includes $73 billion in defense and intelligence funding, $12 billion for agriculture aid and $10 billion for a fund aimed at incentivizing states to adopt Trump-backed voting restrictions, for a total of $95 billion.

The Senate has yet to pass a blueprint of the bill, but it doesn’t include offsets, as of right now — a concern that has been aired by fiscal hawks.

Democrats, meanwhile, took the opportunity to hammer Republicans on the reconciliation bill they muscled through Congress last year, dubbed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Democrats argue that legislation only contributed to the rising deficit.

“Last year, many of us warned that Trump’s reckless budget bill would increase the deficit by trillions — including increasing debt-service costs by $687 billion over the next decade. Those warnings were ignored. And the national debt has now hit $40 trillion,” Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.) said.

Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.), who recently lost his primary, posted in a similar vein , criticizing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act for its effect on the debt.

“If you voted for the Big Beautiful Bill, please don’t get on here and express righteous indignation that the debt is now $40 trillion,” Massie wrote. “Anyone with a room temperature IQ knew that cutting taxes and increasing spending was going to balloon the deficit.”

The minority party also blamed Trump’s ongoing military operation with Iran.

“$40 trillion. For a President and a Republican Party who have railed for years against the nation’s debt, it’s ironic that America is deeper than ever in the red under their leadership. From Trump’s billionaire tax cuts to his war with Iran, it’s clear fiscal responsibility is the last thing on his mind,” Sen. Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) said online.

Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-Mich.) also pointed the finger at Trump.

“Reminder that of the $40 trillion in debt racked up over the course of 250 years and 47 presidents, nearly 30% of it ($11.52 trillion) was added by just one man, Donald Trump, over the course of just a few years,” he said in a post. “Republicans still INSIST that they’re the ones for fiscal responsibility.”

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told “Squawk on the Street” co-host Sara Eisen on CNBC Thursday that he thinks the U.S. can “grow” its way out of the $40 trillion debt.

“But what we do want to signal is I think there’s been a lot of misinformation in terms of what’s going on with the deficit, what’s going on with the deficit to GDP [gross domestic product],” he added.

Bessent said a temporary aspect of the debt is the tariff refunds mandated by the Supreme Court in its ruling in February against Trump’s emergency tariffs. Bessent said U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will implement “the same level of tariffs, and I would expect that our 2026 tariff income is going to be roughly what it was in ’25.”

“But with the Section 301 tariffs, I am confident that we will be back to … the same level if not higher of tariff income for last year,” Bessent later told reporters in front of the White House, where he claimed that despite the $40 trillion milestone, it’s smaller when looking at publicly traded amounts.

articles.title: Moskowitz says Piker, DSA members ‘can’t coexist with me’
articles.summary: Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.) went after left-wing streamer Hasan Piker and members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) on Thursday, saying the two “can’t coexist with me.” “Well, I mean, we’re going to see if we can coexist with them. I mean, they can’t coexist with me.” Moskowitz told Fox Business Network’s Stuart Varney…
articles.body:
Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.) went after left-wing streamer Hasan Piker and members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) on Thursday, saying the two “can’t coexist with me.”

“Well, I mean, we’re going to see if we can coexist with them. I mean, they can’t coexist with me.” Moskowitz told Fox Business Network’s Stuart Varney on “Varney & Co.” while discussing Piker and the DSA.

”They targeted me months ago to try to take me out in a district that Trump won by nine,” he said, referring to President Trump’s 2024 win. “So, that was clear there. They weren’t interested in winning the general election in my seat. They were interested in just taking out a Democrat.”

“And so, you know, look, they’re making blue seats cobalt blue, but we got to win the general election. That should be the goal, and everyone needs to be rowing in that direction,” the congressman added.

On Tuesday, Moskowitz taunted Piker after his primary victory over progressive union organizer Oliver Larkin in Florida’s 25th Congressional District.

In the race, Moskowitz garnered 63.5 percent of the vote to Larkin’s 36.5 percent. The DSA-backed candidate had criticized American military aid for Israel and the war in Gaza, calling it a genocide. Piker fundraised for and backed Larkin.

“My condolences to @hasanthehun,” Moskowitz wrote on social media after his victory .

Piker responded to Moskowitz’s mocking, writing back on social media that it’s “pretty wild that his first thought was a prominent critic of israel, before even thanking his constituents lmao.”

Referencing Moskowitz’s staunch backing of Israel, Piker added that the congressman is “really worried about his genocidal emotional support apartheid state.”

The verbal fire between Piker and Moskowitz reflects the growing divide between the far-left and moderate wings of the party, which has largely focused on disagreements over economic policy and the U.S. stance toward Israel and its war in Gaza.

The Hill has reached out to a contact for Piker and the DSA for comment.

articles.title: Sanders endorses Nixon in Florida Senate race
articles.summary: Progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) is backing Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon (D), who notched an upset victory in Florida’s Senate Democratic primary this week. “Angie Nixon is proof that organized people can take on organized money — and win. Outspent more than 16 to 1, she won in a landslide. Working people all over…
articles.body:
Progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) is backing Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon (D), who notched an upset victory in Florida’s Senate Democratic primary this week.

“Angie Nixon is proof that organized people can take on organized money — and win. Outspent more than 16 to 1, she won in a landslide. Working people all over this country are sick and tired of status quo politics and status quo policies. They want change, real change,” Sanders wrote on social media Thursday afternoon.

Nixon was the first to share the news of the Vermont senator’s endorsement to social media, writing that she was “deeply honored” to have his support.

“Senator Bernie Sanders has been a champion for working people his entire career, and I’m proud to have stood alongside him in 2016 and to carry that fight forward today,” Nixon wrote on social media Thursday.

Nixon, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), achieved a surprise upset Tuesday in the Sunshine State’s Democratic primary for Senate. The state representative beat Alex Vindman, who came to national prominence as a witness in President Trump’s 2019 impeachment hearings, by more than 12 points.

Nixon is set to battle Republican incumbent Sen. Ashley Moody in the fall, both vying to complete the final two years of a Senate term Secretary of State Marco Rubio cut short to join the president’s Cabinet.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) in January 2025 appointed Moody , the state’s former attorney general, to replace Rubio until the next general election.

The Florida state representative’s win this week follows a larger wave of progressive and democratic socialist victories in Democratic primaries across the country. Amid growing division between these candidates and establishment Democrats, Nixon called for party unity in a CBS Mornings appearance Wednesday, saying “people want the same things” despite “labels.”

articles.title: Bond markets rattle economy, sparking controversial buyback
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Bond markets rattle economy, sparking controversial buyback The U.S. bond market is raising alarm bells for the economy, forcing the Trump administration to take emergency measures to ease the immediate impact on American pocketbooks. Yuki Iwamura,…
articles.body:
Bond markets rattle economy, sparking controversial buyback

The U.S. bond market is raising alarm bells for the economy, forcing the Trump administration to take emergency measures to ease the immediate impact on American pocketbooks.

Long-term borrowing costs hit their highest levels across the world on Tuesday, with the cost for the U.S. government to borrow money reaching its highest rate in nearly two decades .

Experts say the unpredictability surrounding the Iran war, President Trump’s erratic trade policies, massive spending on artificial intelligence and the soaring national debt are all contributing to the choppy economic waters.

“One explanation is uncertainty,” said Benjamin Chabot, an adjunct associate professor at Northwestern University and a former senior policy adviser at the Federal Reserve.

“We have a new Fed Chair. We have an FOMC [Federal Open Market Committee] that looks legitimately divided about what the proper policy path is, and that’s largely driven by uncertainty about the economy,” he said.

The yield on the 30-year Treasury bond surpassed 5.3 percent on Tuesday, marking the highest yield since April 2007 — mere months before the start of a financial crisis that upended the global economy in the late 2000s.

The 30-year bond yield ticked down to 5.285 percent at the close of business on Tuesday and dipped to nearly 5.2 percent as of Wednesday afternoon. The yield on the 30-year bond has not closed at under 5 percent since July 6.

The decline in bond yields on Wednesday came after the Treasury Department said it will double the maximum amount of the country’s long-term debt it can buy back.

The increase, from $2 billion to $4 billion per operation, will be in effect from Sept. 9 through at least Nov. 4. The Treasury typically conducts so-called liquidity support buyback operations once or twice a week.

The Hill’s Julia Manchester and Max Rego have more here .

A group of Democrats called for Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh to publicly disclose his communications with President Trump, citing recent reporting they said raises “sincere doubts” about the central bank’s independence from the White House under his leadership.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Thursday said the U.S. can “grow” its way out of the $40 trillion national debt, a milestone reached Wednesday.

US unemployment claims dropped to 206,000 last week with layoffs still sparse

Fewer people applied for U.S. unemployment benefits last week, another sign that layoffs remain low and that most Americans enjoy job security.

Experts say the unpredictability surrounding the Iran war, President Trump’s erratic trade policies, massive spending on artificial intelligence and the soaring national debt are all contributing to the choppy economic waters.
“One explanation is uncertainty,” said Benjamin Chabot, an adjunct associate professor at Northwestern University and a former senior policy adviser at the Federal Reserve.

“We have a new Fed Chair. We have an FOMC [Federal Open Market Committee] that looks legitimately divided about what the proper policy path is, and that’s largely driven by uncertainty about the economy,” he said.

The yield on the 30-year Treasury bond surpassed 5.3 percent on Tuesday, marking the highest yield since April 2007 — mere months before the start of a financial crisis that upended the global economy in the late 2000s.

The 30-year bond yield ticked down to 5.285 percent at the close of business on Tuesday and dipped to nearly 5.2 percent as of Wednesday afternoon. The yield on the 30-year bond has not closed at under 5 percent since July 6.
The decline in bond yields on Wednesday came after the Treasury Department said it will double the maximum amount of the country’s long-term debt it can buy back.

The increase, from $2 billion to $4 billion per operation, will be in effect from Sept. 9 through at least Nov. 4. The Treasury typically conducts so-called liquidity support buyback operations once or twice a week.

articles.title: FBI foils alleged ISIS-inspired bomb plot targeting New York Capitol
articles.summary: Federal police arrested a 35-year-old woman in connection with a plot to bomb the New York State Capitol, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court Thursday. Prosecutors allege in the complaint Jessica Bowie, a resident of Albany, planned to bomb the building and harm officials. They say she told an informant she supported…
articles.body:
Federal police arrested a 35-year-old woman in connection with a plot to bomb the New York State Capitol, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court Thursday.

Prosecutors allege in the complaint Jessica Bowie, a resident of Albany, planned to bomb the building and harm officials. They say she told an informant she supported ISIS before asking for assistance to make explosives.

Bowie is formally charged with one count of attempting to provide material support or resources to a designated foreign terrorist organization. The charge carries a statutory maximum fine of $250,000 and 20 years in prison with a lifetime supervised release.

“Today, the U.S. Department of Justice and FBI announced the arrest of an individual who allegedly plotted an attack on the New York State Capitol,” New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) wrote in a Wednesday statement posted to social platform X.

“While there is no immediate threat at this time, we will continue working closely with our law enforcement partners to protect New Yorkers and keep our communities safe,” she concluded.

FBI special agent Joshua Parker, assigned to the Joint Terrorism Task Force in Albany, detailed in the complaint how Bowie was identified as a suspect and the a sting operation to arrest her.

Bowie reportedly converted to Islam five years ago and formally made an oath of allegiance to ISIS in May.

An FBI informant communicated with Bowie from July 16 to Aug. 17, revealing that Bowie messaged that she wanted to “target my state capitol” which was “less than two miles” from her home. Within this time frame, she allegedly walked around the New York State Capitol approximately five separate times.

Other accounts that police tied to Bowie messaged users in Arabic saying, “Praise to be Allah for September 11th” and “When I can migrate, I will poison these infidels.”

She met with two other informants in person, who recorded the meeting. In that meeting, she allegedly indicated she wanted to target other prominent buildings in the future such as the White House.

“As alleged, Bowie plotted to deploy an explosive device at the New York State Capitol … before fleeing to ISIS‑controlled territory in Syria,” Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg said Thursday .

The complaint stated she told agents in an interview after her arrest, “There’s no helping me. You guys know enough, there’s no helping me, I’m … going to prison for the rest of my life.”

articles.title: Rogers courts Democrats in Michigan Senate race
articles.summary: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers officially launched the “Democrats for Mike Rogers” coalition on Thursday, two months out from the general election. Rogers made the announcement of the coalition at an event that featured a handful of Democrats including Michigan state Rep. Karen Whitsett (D). “Michiganders are tired of anger and division, and I…
articles.body:
Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers officially launched the “Democrats for Mike Rogers” coalition on Thursday, two months out from the general election.

Rogers made the announcement of the coalition at an event that featured a handful of Democrats including Michigan state Rep. Karen Whitsett (D).

“Michiganders are tired of anger and division, and I don’t think there’s a better representation of that than what you see standing here today,” Rogers said on Thursday.

“When the stakes are this high, you put your differences aside, you listen to each other, and you work together. That’s what Michigan needs now more than ever. This election is bigger than Republican versus Democrat, left versus right,” he added.

Rogers’s comments come as his opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed leads in the polls across the Great Lakes State, as he pushes for Medicare for All and rejects ties to corporate PACs.

President Trump has endorsed Rogers, who was a former Republican lawmaker in the House. While serving in the lower chamber, he opposed abortion and pushed to end Affordable Care Act provisions.

Comparatively, El-Sayed is a doctor and has backed the Medicare for All initiative supported by progressives nationwide.

Whitsett said at the Thursday event that she would vote for the Republican nominee after falsely alleging that voters would lose access to healthcare if Medicare for All was implemented.

“I’m not standing here as a state representative. I’m not standing here as a Democrat or a Republican, because I’m neither. My bottom line is that I want people to start to understand you need to pick your candidate by your issue. Period,” Whisett said.

Under current Medicare for All proposals, private duplicate health insurance like Blue Cross and Blue Shield and Aetna would be phased out and replaced with automatic enrollment in a universal public government program instead.

“Once again, you say you don’t want the government in your business. Well, the government will be controlling your healthcare. They will control your doctors. They will control your medication. They will control your visits. They will control everything. So, if for no other reason, common sense prevails that Mike Rogers is the candidate for you,” she added.

El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to The Hill’s request for comment regarding Rogers’s new democratic coalition.

articles.title: Progressive wins special election to fill Swalwell’s California House seat
articles.summary: Progressive California state Sen. Aisha Wahab (D) is projected to defeat Bay Area Rapid Transit Board President Melissa Hernandez in the special election to fill the remainder of former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s (D-Calif.) term in the House, according to Decision Desk HQ. Swalwell, once seen as the front-runner in the California governor’s race, dropped out…
articles.body:
Progressive California state Sen. Aisha Wahab (D) is projected to defeat Bay Area Rapid Transit Board President Melissa Hernandez in the special election to fill the remainder of former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s (D-Calif.) term in the House, according to Decision Desk HQ.

Swalwell, once seen as the front-runner in the California governor’s race, dropped out from the contest and left his seat amid sexual assault allegations, which the congressman has denied.

Wahab and Hernandez placed into the special election following the initial June primary.

Wahab’s victory is not entirely surprising given that the progressive handily led Hernandez in the primary for the special election by 26 percentage points.

The two are also vying for the full two-year term for the Alameda County-based 14th Congressional District; Wahab led Hernandez in the primary for the full two-year term by 21 points.

Wahab’s win also marks a major defeat for the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s (AIPAC) super PAC, which was one of several groups to spend in the race to support Hernandez and oppose Wahab.

The race has notably seen large outside spending for a reliably Democratic House seat: United Democracy Project (UDP), AIPAC’s super PAC, has spent roughly $2.5 million to support Hernandez and oppose Wahab. Bold America, which was launched by several former members of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and whose group has received money from UDP, has spent about $1.8 million .

Safer Alameda County PAC has separately spent just shy of $500,000 .

Meanwhile, a separate group, American Priorities, has spent about $100,000 to support Wahab and oppose Hernandez. The super PAC for the progressive Jewish group J Street has also spent just more than $100,000 to support Wahab.

Support over Israel has become an unexpected focal point in the race with Wahab opposing unconditional aid to Israel and deeming the events unfolding in Gaza a “genocide.”

During a candidate forum, Hernandez had declined to call the events in Gaza a “genocide,” saying “Israel had the right to defend itself” following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack against Israel. However, she added that “the destruction into Gaza has gone too far.”

The race also became increasingly personal and nasty. A supporter of Hernandez directed a Federal Elections Commission (FEC) complaint toward Wahab, alleging that her senatorial committee gave money to a county local party that then turned around and spent it toward her congressional bid.

Wahab told The Hill she hasn’t heard from the FEC and said that “until the FEC actually takes action, this is nothing more than a political allegation being pushed by our opponents.” Alameda County Democratic Central Committee said in a statement that it was aware of the complaint and maintained that it has been “in compliance with federal election laws.”

Meanwhile, Wahab has launched her own FEC complaint after seeing a number of social media posts her campaign has called defamatory. Her campaign is looking to see where those posts are being created to influence her primary and whether they should be reported as such.

Wahab and Hernandez will face off again in November for the full two-year term.

articles.title: Wetlands policy causes GOP friction
articles.summary: {beacon} Energy & Environment Energy & Environment The Big Story Cramer puts hold on Trump nominees over wetlands Republican Sen. Kevin Cramer (N.D.) is placing a hold on all future Trump nominees over the administration’s approach to wetlands. © Greg Nash In a statement shared with The Hill, Cramer expressed disappointment that the administration is leaving…
articles.body:
Cramer puts hold on Trump nominees over wetlands

Republican Sen. Kevin Cramer (N.D.) is placing a hold on all future Trump nominees over the administration’s approach to wetlands.

In a statement shared with The Hill, Cramer expressed disappointment that the administration is leaving a Biden-era wetland policy in place for the time being — and indicated that he would not advance the president’s nominees as a result.

“The blind defense of a Biden rule favored by environmental extremists at the expense of farmers confounds me, particularly at a time when our ag producers are hurting so badly,” he said.

“My farmers are furious and so am I. There won’t be another nominee confirmed until something changes,” he said.

The holds were first reported by E&E News .

Holds can slow the process of confirming nominees, requiring the Senate to spend hours debating them and taking additional votes for each nominee.

Cramer’s hold comes as the Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) decided not to move forward with changes to a Biden-era policy that sought to prevent the draining of wetlands that were protected under conservation easements — thereby protecting duck habitat.

articles.title: Schwartz recognizes CDC strife in first talks with staff
articles.summary: Click in for more news from The Hill {beacon} Healthcare Healthcare The Big Story Schwartz recognizes CDC strife in first talks with staff Erica Schwartz, the newly confirmed director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), acknowledged the agency she is now tasked with leading faces an uphill battle in terms of…
articles.body:
Schwartz recognizes CDC strife in first talks with staff

Erica Schwartz, the newly confirmed director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), acknowledged the agency she is now tasked with leading faces an uphill battle in terms of morale in her first conversation with staffers.

Schwartz was confirmed after roughly a year of the CDC lacking official leadership, former CDC Director Susan Monarez having been fired after less than a month. She inherits leadership over an agency that saw massive layoffs last year as well as a fatal shooting at its headquarters in Atlanta.

In a recording of an all-staff meeting obtained by The Hill, Schwartz acknowledged that morale within the agency is struggling .

“I am here asking you to give me the benefit of the doubt and to work with me as I go through our listening sessions to help me rebuild the trust that may have been lost,” Schwartz said when asked for her plans to improve staffer morale.

“In order to build morale, I think the fundamental thing that I have to work on with all of you is to help you understand that I want to earn your trust, and that I will do what I need to do to earn your trust,” she added.

Another staffer asked Schwartz what she believed should be improved or rebuilt at the CDC.

“You guys are feeling this weight, and I’m so sorry for that. I’m sorry that you have to live under this extreme psychological unsafety, and I apologize for that,” Schwartz said, noting one staffer had shared that they are nervous to ask questions due to a fear of being reprimanded.

Several staffers at the CDC were concerned with how Schwartz planned to handle vaccine policy , in light of the agency’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) being disbanded by a federal judge earlier this year and President Trump’s executive order to split up the MMR vaccine and reduce the number of childhood immunizations.

Schwartz said she would work to ensure the CDC had input in implementing Trump’s executive order.

“My understanding — we are going to be looking at that executive order. Does it make sense? What are the pieces that we like? What are the pieces that we don’t like? And then when ACIP is reconstituted, we can have that body of information that we can share with ACIP, and ACIP can say this is ridiculous, or they can say this is actually really good, and we’ll use pieces of it,” said Schwartz.

“You guys are feeling this weight, and I’m so sorry for that. I’m sorry that you have to live under this extreme psychological unsafety, and I apologize for that,” Schwartz said, noting one staffer had shared that they are nervous to ask questions due to a fear of being reprimanded.

Several staffers at the CDC were concerned with how Schwartz planned to handle vaccine policy , in light of the agency’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) being disbanded by a federal judge earlier this year and President Trump’s executive order to split up the MMR vaccine and reduce the number of childhood immunizations.
Schwartz said she would work to ensure the CDC had input in implementing Trump’s executive order.

“My understanding — we are going to be looking at that executive order. Does it make sense? What are the pieces that we like? What are the pieces that we don’t like? And then when ACIP is reconstituted, we can have that body of information that we can share with ACIP, and ACIP can say this is ridiculous, or they can say this is actually really good, and we’ll use pieces of it,” said Schwartz.

articles.summary: {beacon} Technology Technology The Big Story Mike Rogers calls for one-year data center moratorium Former Rep. articles.body:
Mike Rogers calls for one-year data center moratorium

Former Rep. Mike Rogers, the GOP nominee in a critical Senate battle in Michigan, on Thursday called for a one-year pause on data center construction, the latest sign of the political toxicity of the server warehouses fueling the AI boom.

Rogers said in a statement that he is pushing for a yearlong moratorium on new data centers “until we establish a fair, transparent approval process that puts local communities first.”

“While I don’t support a federal ban, Michigan needs stronger guardrails to protect community control, prevent utility price hikes, protect our water and stop pay-to-play schemes,” he added.

His opponent, Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed , has previously waded into the data center debate, putting forward a series of “terms of engagement” for new projects.

This includes requiring developers to cover any increased energy costs and commit to using closed-loop cooling systems, among other provisions.

“Unless and until we have those terms of engagement at the federal level, I stand with local and state elected officials saying that we cannot approve any more of these until we have federal level guardrails,” El-Sayed said in July during an appearance alongside local organizers at a data center construction site.

The Michigan race is critical to both parties’ hopes of holding the Senate majority in the next Congress. Democrats need to pick up four seats to win the majority, but that is assuming they hold on to the Michigan seat that retiring Sen. Gary Peters (D) now holds.

Data centers are playing an increasingly prominent role in midterm races across the country as Americans have grow increasigly wary of the push to rapidly build more AI infrastructure.

articles.title: US approves possible $4.5 billion sale of refueling aircraft to Qatar
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Defense & NatSec newsletter {beacon} Defense &National Security Defense &National Security The Big Story US approves $4.5 billion sale of refueling planes to Qatar The U.S. approved on Thursday a possible $4.5 billion sale of four aerial refueling aircraft and related equipment to Qatar. Christopher Pike, Bloomberg via Getty Images…
articles.body:
US approves $4.5 billion sale of refueling planes to Qatar

The U.S. approved on Thursday a possible $4.5 billion sale of four aerial refueling aircraft and related equipment to Qatar.

Christopher Pike, Bloomberg via Getty Images

The State Department greenlighted the potential sale of four KC-46A refueling aircraft , a deal which could include eight PW4062 turbofan engines (four installed and four to spare), ten AN/ALR-69A radar warning receivers, 15 Guardian Laser Transmitter Assemblies and eight LAIRCM system processor replacements, the department said in a release.

“The proposed sale will increase Qatar’s capability to meet current and future threats by enhancing its defense capabilities and interoperability with U.S. and allied forces and reinforcing Qatar’s strategic role in regional security,” the department’s Bureau of Political-Military Affairs said. “Qatar will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces.”

The deal also encompasses missile warning sensors, cartridge-actuated devices, propellant-actuated devices; control interface units, user data module cards, electronic warfare database support, KIV-77 crypto module, KY-100M crypto terminals and other parts.

The deal is not final, as Congress could put a pause on the transaction.

The announcement comes as U.S. allies in the Gulf have faced heavy attacks from Iran since the war between Washington and Tehran began in late February.

Iran has fired ballistic and cruise missiles and one-way attack drones at Gulf states, including Qatar.

“The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the basic military balance in the region, the department said on Thursday.
